objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked on XDG MIME database reload events. The callback receives a single opaque user_data pointer that was supplied during registration.
Function pointer type for a destructor/cleanup function paired with a registered callback. It is called with the same user_data when the callback is removed or when the system is shut down.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_mime_type_for_data
functions.signature: const char *xdg_mime_get_mime_type_for_data (const void *data, size_t len, int *result_prio);
functions.description: Determines the best-guess MIME type for a memory buffer. Intended for sniffing raw data; optionally returns a detection priority via result_prio if supported. Returns a pointer to an internal, NUL-terminated MIME type string (e.g., "text/plain").
requirements: data must point to at least len readable bytes.
len specifies the number of bytes available at data; use xdg_mime_get_max_buffer_extents() to know how many bytes are maximally inspected.
result_prio: usage and NULL-ability are not documented in this header; behavior is unknown if NULL.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_mime_type_for_file
functions.description: Determines the MIME type for a filesystem path using file name, metadata and/or content as available. Returns a pointer to an internal, NUL-terminated MIME type string.
requirements: file_name must be a valid NUL-terminated path string.
statbuf: header does not document whether NULL is allowed; if provided, it must point to a valid struct stat filled for file_name; NULL-ability is unknown.
Returned const char* is not owned by the caller; do not free.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_mime_type_from_file_name
functions.description: Guesses MIME type from a file name (typically by extension and known patterns) without reading file contents. Returns an internal, NUL-terminated MIME type string.
requirements: file_name must be a valid NUL-terminated string (path or base name).
Returned const char* is not owned by the caller; do not free.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_mime_types_from_file_name
functions.signature: int xdg_mime_get_mime_types_from_file_name (const char *file_name, const char *mime_types[], int n_mime_types);
functions.description: Retrieves multiple candidate MIME types for a file name (e.g., for ambiguous extensions), storing up to n_mime_types entries into mime_types. Returns the number of MIME types written or required (implementation-defined).
requirements: file_name must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
mime_types must be a writable array with capacity for at least n_mime_types elements; each element receives a const char* pointer (internal strings; do not free).
n_mime_types must be >= 0.
Ownership of the returned pointers remains with the library; do not modify or free them.

functions.name: xdg_mime_is_valid_mime_type
functions.description: Checks whether a MIME type string is syntactically valid and/or known to the database. Returns non-zero if valid, zero otherwise.
requirements: mime_type must be a valid NUL-terminated string (e.g., "type/subtype").
Return semantics beyond non-zero/zero are not further documented here.

functions.name: xdg_mime_mime_type_equal
functions.description: Compares two MIME type strings for equality (considering aliases as applicable). Returns non-zero if equal, zero otherwise.
requirements: mime_a and mime_b must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
Return value is an int used as boolean (non-zero equals true).

functions.name: xdg_mime_media_type_equal
functions.description: Checks whether two MIME types share the same top-level media type (the part before '/'). Returns non-zero if media types match, zero otherwise.
requirements: mime_a and mime_b must be valid NUL-terminated MIME strings containing '/'.
Behavior for malformed inputs is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: xdg_mime_mime_type_subclass
functions.description: Determines whether mime_a is a subclass (or derived/child) of mime_b according to the MIME hierarchy/aliases. Returns non-zero if true, zero otherwise.
requirements: mime_a and mime_b must be valid NUL-terminated strings representing MIME types.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_mime_parents
functions.description: Deprecated: Returns an array of parent MIME types for mime. The header notes this does not work correctly with caches; prefer xdg_mime_list_mime_parents(). Returned array ownership and lifetime are not documented here; treat as internal.
requirements: mime must be a valid NUL-terminated MIME type string.
Function is deprecated; callers should migrate to xdg_mime_list_mime_parents().
Because ownership is unclear, do not free the returned array unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: xdg_mime_list_mime_parents
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated NULL-terminated array of parent MIME types for mime. The caller is expected to free the array it returns (as per the header note).
requirements: mime must be a valid NUL-terminated MIME type string.

The returned char** array is heap-allocated; the caller must free it. Element ownership (whether to free each string) is not specified here; at minimum free the array pointer; freeing elements is unknown without further docs.

functions.name: xdg_mime_unalias_mime_type
functions.description: Maps a MIME type to its canonical (unalias) form using the database. Returns a pointer to an internal, NUL-terminated canonical MIME type string.
requirements: mime must be a valid NUL-terminated MIME type string.
Returned const char* is not owned by the caller; do not free.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_icon
functions.description: Gets the icon name associated with a MIME type, if any. Returns a pointer to an internal, NUL-terminated string representing an icon name or possibly NULL/empty if none (exact behavior not specified here).
requirements: mime must be a valid NUL-terminated MIME type string.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, is not owned by the caller; do not free.
Whether NULL can be returned is not specified; handle defensively.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_generic_icon
functions.description: Gets a generic icon name for the top-level media of a MIME type (e.g., "text-x-generic"). Returns a pointer to an internal, NUL-terminated string or possibly NULL if none (not specified).
requirements: mime must be a valid NUL-terminated MIME type string.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, is not owned by the caller; do not free.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_simple_globs
functions.signature: int xdg_mime_get_simple_globs (const char *mime, char *globs[], int n_globs);
functions.description: Retrieves simple filename glob patterns associated with a MIME type, storing up to n_globs strings into globs. Returns the number of globs written or required (implementation-defined).
requirements: mime must be a valid NUL-terminated MIME type string.
globs must be a writable array with capacity for at least n_globs elements; each receives a char* (ownership not specified here).
n_globs must be >= 0.
Ownership/lifetime of strings stored in globs is not documented; treat them as internal unless otherwise specified and do not free.

functions.name: xdg_mime_get_max_buffer_extents
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of bytes of data that may be inspected when determining file type by content. Useful to size buffers for xdg_mime_get_mime_type_for_data().
requirements: No arguments; safe to call anytime after library initialization (implicit).
Return value semantics beyond being a non-negative size are not documented here.

functions.name: xdg_mime_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down and frees internal resources of the XDG MIME system, potentially invalidating previously returned pointers. Intended for process/library teardown.
requirements: Should be called when MIME routines are no longer needed; calling afterward may invalidate previously returned internal pointers.
Do not use other functions that rely on internal caches after shutdown unless reinitialized implicitly (unspecified here).

functions.name: xdg_mime_dump
functions.description: Dumps internal state or database contents for debugging. Exact output and destination are not specified in this header.
requirements: No arguments; intended for diagnostics/debugging.
May produce output to stdout/stderr or logs; unspecified here.

functions.name: xdg_mime_register_reload_callback
functions.signature: int xdg_mime_register_reload_callback (XdgMimeCallback callback, void *data, XdgMimeDestroy destroy);
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when the MIME database is reloaded. Returns an integer callback ID that can be used to remove the callback later. destroy, if non-NULL, will be called with data when the callback is removed or on shutdown.
requirements: callback must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(void*).
data is passed back to callback and destroy as-is; must remain valid for the lifetime of the registration.
destroy may be NULL or a valid function pointer to clean up user data; if provided, it must tolerate being called exactly once when the registration is removed or on shutdown.
The returned callback ID must be stored to allow removal with xdg_mime_remove_callback().

functions.name: xdg_mime_remove_callback
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered reload callback by its ID. If a destroy function was provided at registration, it will be called to clean up user data.
requirements: callback_id must be a valid ID previously returned by xdg_mime_register_reload_callback().
Safe to call at most once per registered ID; behavior for invalid or repeated IDs is not documented.

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for arbitrary binary data to feed xdg_mime_get_mime_type_for_data.
# Strategy:
# - Produce realistic file signatures (magic numbers) and short headers for many common formats
#   to drive positive identifications.
# - Vary sizes, include edge cases (very short, exactly typical sniff-lengths, etc.).
# - Include combinations with text content, UTF-8 BOMs, shebangs, XML/HTML, JSON, etc.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic with the provided seed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Common magic numbers and minimal valid-looking payloads for various formats
# Each entry is a callable that returns bytes. These snippets should be valid-looking
# so the sniffer can plausibly recognize them.
def _png(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # PNG signature + minimal IHDR chunk + IEND
    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    # Minimal IHDR: 13 bytes data, 4 length, 'IHDR', data, CRC
    # We'll embed a tiny 1x1 RGBA IHDR with placeholder CRCs (many sniffers ignore CRC)
    ihdr = (b"\x00\x00\x00\x0dIHDR" +
            b"\x00\x00\x00\x01" +  # width 1
            b"\x00\x00\x00\x01" +  # height 1
            b"\x08" +                # bit depth 8
            b"\x06" +                # color type RGBA
            b"\x00\x00\x00" +      # compression, filter, interlace
            b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")   # fake CRC
    iend = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00IEND\xaeB`\x82"
    return sig + ihdr + iend

def _jpeg(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # JPEG with SOI, APP0 JFIF, DQT, SOF0 minimal
    data = bytearray()
    data += b"\xff\xd8"  # SOI
    data += b"\xff\xe0"  # APP0
    data += b"\x00\x10"  # length
    data += b"JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"
    data += b"\xff\xdb\x00C" + b"\x00"*0x43  # DQT
    data += b"\xff\xc0\x00\x11\x08\x00\x01\x00\x01\x03\x01\x11\x00\x02\x11\x01\x03\x11\x01"
    data += b"\xff\xda\x00\x0c\x03\x01\x00\x02\x11\x03\x11\x00?\x00"  # SOS
    data += b"\x00"*16
    data += b"\xff\xd9"  # EOI
    return bytes(data)

def _gif(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    hdr = rnd.choice([b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a"]) + b"\x01\x00\x01\x00\x80\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\xff,\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00\x02\x02D\x01\x00;"
    return hdr

def _pdf(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ver = rnd.choice([b"1.3", b"1.4", b"1.5", b"1.7"])
    return b"%PDF-" + ver + b"\n%\xe2\xe3\xcf\xd3\n1 0 obj<<>>endobj\nstartxref\n0\n%%EOF\n"

def _zip(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal local file header (no data) + central dir
    name = b"test.txt"
    lf = (b"PK\x03\x04" + b"\x14\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" +
          struct.pack("<HHH", len(name), 0, 0) + name)
    cd = (b"PK\x01\x02" + b"\x14\x00\x14\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" +
          b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00" + struct.pack("<HHH", len(name), 0, 0) +
          b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00" + name)
    eocd = b"PK\x05\x06\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00" + struct.pack("<IIH", len(cd), len(lf), 0) + b"\x00\x00"
    return lf + cd + eocd

def _gzip(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal gzip header + empty DEFLATE block sequence (not fully valid but enough for magic)
    return b"\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff" + b"\x03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"

def _tar(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # USTAR header magic at offset 257
    buf = bytearray(512)
    name = b"file.txt\x00"
    buf[:len(name)] = name
    buf[257:257+6] = b"ustar\x00"
    buf[263:263+2] = b"00"
    return bytes(buf)

def _elf(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # ELF header
    ei_class = rnd.choice([1, 2])
    data = bytearray(b"\x7fELF")
    data += bytes([ei_class, 1, 1]) + b"\x00"*9
    data += b"\x00"*48
    return bytes(data)

def _pe(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # DOS header + PE signature
    data = bytearray(b"MZ" + b"\x00"*58)
    data += struct.pack("<I", 0x80)  # e_lfanew (offset to PE)
    pad = 0x80 - len(data)
    data += b"\x00"*pad
    data += b"PE\x00\x00" + b"\x4c\x01\x00\x00" + b"\x00"*20
    return bytes(data)

def _mp3(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # ID3v2 header or frame sync
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return b"ID3\x03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x10" + b"\x00"*16
    else:
        return b"\xff\xfb\x90\x64" + b"\x00"*32

def _wav(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"RIFF" + struct.pack("<I", 36) + b"WAVEfmt \x10\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x40\x1f\x00\x00\x80>\x00\x00\x02\x00\x10\x00data\x00\x00\x00\x00"

def _ogg(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"OggS" + b"\x00"*22

def _bmp(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"BM" + b"\x36\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x003\x00\x00\x00(\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x18\x00" + b"\x00"*16

def _ico(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x10\x10\x00\x00\x01\x00\x04\x00\x28\x01\x00\x00\x16\x00\x00\x00"

def _rar(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"Rar!\x1a\x07\x00" + b"\x00"*8

def _sevenz(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"7zXZ\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"[:6]  # start with 7z magic

def _xz(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\xfd7zXZ\x00" + b"\x00"*10

def _xml(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    decl = rnd.choice([b"<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n", b"\xef\xbb\xbf<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n"]) \
        if rnd.random() < 0.7 else b""
    body = b"<root><child attr=\"val\">text</child></root>\n"
    return decl + body

def _html(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    start = rnd.choice([b"<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\"></head><body>", b"<html><body>"])
    end = b"</body></html>\n"
    return start + b"Hello\n" + end

def _json(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"{\n  \"name\": \"value\",\n  \"list\": [1, 2, 3]\n}\n"

def _javascript(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    she = b"#!/usr/bin/env node\n" if rnd.random() < 0.3 else b""
    return she + b"console.log(\"hello\");\n"

def _shell(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    she = rnd.choice([b"#!/bin/sh\n", b"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n"]) if rnd.random() < 0.8 else b""
    return she + b"echo hello\n"

def _python_script(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    she = b"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n" if rnd.random() < 0.9 else b""
    return she + b"print('hi')\n"

def _plain_text(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Include UTF-8 BOM sometimes
    bom = b"\xef\xbb\xbf" if rnd.random() < 0.2 else b""
    lines = [b"This is a line.", b"Another line.", b"End."]
    rnd.shuffle(lines)
    return bom + b"\n".join(lines) + b"\n"

def _csv(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    header = b"id,name,value\n"
    rows = [f"{i},name{i},{rnd.randint(0,100)}\n".encode() for i in range(1, rnd.randint(2,5))]
    return header + b"".join(rows)

def _ini(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"[section]\nkey=value\nflag=true\n"

def _rtf(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"{\\rtf1\\ansi\n{\\fonttbl \\f0 Courier;}\n\\f0 text}\n"

def _sqlite(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"SQLite format 3\x00" + b"\x00"*80

def _classfile(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\xca\xfe\xba\xbe" + b"\x00\x34\x00\x00" + b"\x00"*32

def _wasm(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00asm\x01\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00"*8

def _pcap(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\xd4\xc3\xb2\xa1\x02\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00"

def _heif(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # ISO-BMFF brand
    return b"\x00\x00\x00\x18ftypheic\x00\x00\x00\x00heicmif1"

def _iso_bmff_mp4(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00\x00\x00\x18ftypisom\x00\x00\x02\x00isomiso2"

def _text_xml_svg(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"<?xml version=\"1.0\"?><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"></svg>\n"

def _protobuf(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # No fixed magic; create plausible binary with low ASCII content
    return bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rnd.randint(16, 64)))

def _random_binary(rnd: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

GENERATORS = [
    _png, _jpeg, _gif, _pdf, _zip, _gzip, _tar, _elf, _pe, _mp3,
    _wav, _ogg, _bmp, _ico, _rar, _sevenz, _xz, _xml, _html, _json,
    _javascript, _shell, _python_script, _plain_text, _csv, _ini, _rtf,
    _sqlite, _classfile, _wasm, _pcap, _heif, _iso_bmff_mp4, _text_xml_svg,
    _protobuf
]

# Some extensions to append sometimes to bias filename-based sniffers if used elsewhere.
FILENAME_HINTS = [
    b"\n--filename:.png\n", b"\n--filename:.jpg\n", b"\n--filename:.gif\n",
    b"\n--filename:.pdf\n", b"\n--filename:.zip\n", b"\n--filename:.mp3\n",
    b"\n--filename:.txt\n", b"\n--filename:.html\n", b"\n--filename:.xml\n",
]

# Compose different buffers: exact magic-only, magic+padding, text plus binary, etc.
def _compose(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base_gen = rnd.choice(GENERATORS)
    base = base_gen(rnd)

    # Decide final target size: include short (1-32), medium (64-512), long (1024-4096)
    size_class = rnd.random()
    if size_class < 0.2:
        target = rnd.randint(1, 32)
    elif size_class < 0.8:
        target = rnd.randint(64, 512)
    else:
        target = rnd.randint(1024, MAX_SIZE)

    # Optionally prepend or append whitespace/newlines for text-like formats
    if any(base.startswith(prefix) for prefix in [b"<?xml", b"<!DOCTYPE", b"<html", b"{", b"#!/", b"console.", b"SQLite "]):
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            base = b"\n"*rnd.randint(1,3) + base
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            base = base + b"\n"*rnd.randint(1,3)

    # Optionally append filename hint marker (still valid for content sniffers; just extra bytes)
    if rnd.random() < 0.15 and len(base) < target:
        base += rnd.choice(FILENAME_HINTS)

    # Pad or trim to target length, using structured padding for text vs binary
    if len(base) < target:
        remaining = target - len(base)
        if base[:1] in [b"<", b"{", b"/", b"#", b"c", b"S", b"\xef"] or base.startswith((b"<?xml", b"<!DOCTYPE", b"<html")):
            pad = (b"\n" + b" ") * (remaining // 2) + b"\n" * (remaining % 2)
            pad = pad[:remaining]
        else:
            pad = _random_binary(rnd, remaining)
        base = base + pad
    elif len(base) > target:
        base = base[:target]

    return base


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes emit very small or empty buffers to test edge handling (but non-empty preferred)
    mode = rnd.random()
    if mode < 0.05:
        # Empty or 1-byte buffers
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            return b""
        else:
            return bytes([rnd.randrange(256)])

    # Most of the time, generate composed, valid-looking data
    buf = _compose(rnd)

    # Ensure not exceeding MAX_SIZE
    if len(buf) > MAX_SIZE:
        buf = buf[:MAX_SIZE]

    return buf

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator builds a realistic filesystem path with an extension and
# file content that matches the extension, so that the target fuzzer stub
# can stat() the file and the library can infer a MIME type from its name
# and possibly its content.
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in the stub points to a filename with random fuzzable data.
# Many fuzz frameworks create the file at that path with the provided bytes as its content.
# We therefore encode a path string followed by a NUL, then the file bytes.
# A common convention is: buffer = path + "\0" + content.
# This script adheres to that convention. It avoids I/O and external deps.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Minimal file signatures and representative contents for popular types
MAGICS = {
    "png": bytes.fromhex("89504E470D0A1A0A") +
            b"\x00\x00\x00\rIHDR" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x10\x00\x00\x00\x10\x08\x02\x00\x00\x00" +
            b"\x00\x00\x00\x00IEND\xaeB`\x82",
    "jpg": bytes.fromhex("FFD8FFE000104A46494600010100000100010000") + b"\xFF\xD9",

EXT_PRIORITIES = [
    ("txt", [".txt", ".text", ".asc"]),
    ("html", [".html", ".htm"]),
    ("xml", [".xml"]),
    ("json", [".json"]),
    ("csv", [".csv"]),

    ("ogg", [".ogg"]),

]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=10) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_dirs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    depth = rng.choices([0,1,2,3], weights=[2,3,3,2], k=1)[0]
    dirs = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        d = _rand_name(rng)
        dirs.append(d)
    return dirs

def _choose_type_and_ext(rng: random.Random):
    kind, exts = rng.choice(EXT_PRIORITIES)
    ext = rng.choice(exts)
    return kind, ext

def _content_for(kind: str, rng: random.Random, size_limit: int) -> bytes:
    base = MAGICS.get(kind, b"")
    # Expand with plausible padding for certain types
    if kind in {"txt", "html", "xml", "json", "csv", "ini", "js", "css", "svg"}:
        # Add some random textual content
        extra_lines = rng.randint(0, 20)
        blob = [base]
        for _ in range(extra_lines):
            line_len = rng.randint(5, 60)
            line = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_.,:;/#{}()[]<>") for _ in range(line_len))
            blob.append(line.encode('utf-8') + b"\n")
            if sum(len(x) for x in blob) > size_limit:
                break
        data = b''.join(blob)
    else:
        # For binary, pad with random bytes but stay within size_limit
        data = base
        pad_target = rng.randint(0, max(0, size_limit - len(base)))
        data += rng.randbytes(pad_target) if pad_target > 0 else b""
    return data[:size_limit]

def _build_path(rng: random.Random, ext: str) -> str:
    # Construct relative or absolute path variably
    is_abs = rng.random() < 0.3
    parts = _rand_dirs(rng)
    fname_base = _rand_name(rng, 1, 12)
    # Occasionally include dots for multi-dot names
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        fname_base += "." + _rand_name(rng, 1, 6)
    fname = fname_base + ext
    if is_abs:
        path = os.sep + os.sep.join(parts + [fname]) if parts else os.sep + fname
    else:
        # Sometimes include current dir or parent dir notations
        prefix = []
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            prefix.append(".")
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            prefix.append("..")
        path_parts = prefix + parts + [fname]
        path = os.path.join(*path_parts)
    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    kind, ext = _choose_type_and_ext(rng)
    path = _build_path(rng, ext)

    # Budget bytes: path + NUL + content <= MAX_TOTAL
    # Reserve at least some bytes for content
    max_content = MAX_TOTAL - (len(path.encode('utf-8')) + 1)
    max_content = max(0, min(max_content, 2048))

    content = _content_for(kind, rng, max_content)

    # Compose as: path\0content so the fuzz harness can parse a filename and content
    out = path.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00" + content

    return out[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for interesting filename/path strings to exercise extension-based MIME logic.
# Focus: xdg_mime_get_mime_type_from_file_name, xdg_mime_get_mime_types_from_file_name
# Requirements: return bytes representing a NUL-terminated string-like buffer (FUZZ framework
# will read as std::string via FUZZ_PARAM_STR). We thus just provide bytes content; fuzzer will
# convert. Keep <= 4096 bytes.

COMMON_EXTS = [
    # Text and code
    "txt", "md", "rtf", "csv", "tsv", "json", "jsonl", "yaml", "yml", "xml", "html", "htm",
    "css", "js", "mjs", "ts", "tsx", "c", "cc", "cpp", "cxx", "h", "hpp", "hh", "java",
    "class", "jar", "py", "pyc", "ipynb", "rb", "go", "rs", "php", "sh", "bash", "zsh",
    # Images
    "png", "jpg", "jpeg", "gif", "bmp", "tiff", "tif", "webp", "heic", "ico", "svg",
    # Audio/Video
    "mp3", "flac", "wav", "ogg", "oga", "m4a", "aac", "opus", "mp4", "m4v", "mkv", "avi",
    # Archives/Compressed
    "zip", "tar", "gz", "bz2", "xz", "zst", "7z", "rar", "tar.gz", "tar.bz2", "tar.xz",
    # Docs
    "pdf", "ps", "epub", "azw3", "doc", "docx", "xls", "xlsx", "ppt", "pptx",
    # Fonts
    "ttf", "otf", "woff", "woff2",
    # Executables/Scripts
    "exe", "dll", "so", "dylib", "appimage", "run", "bat", "cmd", "com",
    # System/Config
    "conf", "ini", "desktop", "service", "socket", "mount", "fstab",
    # Emails/Web
    "eml", "ics", "vcard", "vcf",
    # Misc
    "db", "sqlite", "sqlite3", "log", "lock", "bak", "tmp", "swp",
]

# Special filenames and edge cases
EDGE_BASENAMES = [
    "a",  # minimal non-empty
    ".", "..",  # path traversal names
    ".hidden",  # hidden without extension
    ".bashrc", ".profile", ".gitignore", ".gitattributes",
    "Makefile", "Dockerfile", "README", "LICENSE", "CHANGELOG",
    "CON", "NUL", "PRN", "AUX", "COM1", "LPT1",  # reserved on Windows
    "archive.tar.gz",  # compound extension
    "music.flac:Zone.Identifier",  # NTFS ADS-like
    "photo.jpeg;param=foo",  # MIME-like params in name
]

# Path components including Unicode and tricky bytes
UNICODE_NAMES = [
    "Δοκιμή", "ファイル", "文件", "файл", "ملف", "archivo", "fichier", "daten",
    "スペース", "空 白", "emoji_😀", "ñoño", "naïve", "résumé", "straße",
]

DIR_COMPONENTS = [
    "home", "usr", "bin", "var", "tmp", "etc", "opt", "mnt", "media", "dev",
    "Program Files", "Users", "AppData", "桌面", "デスクトップ",
]

PREFIXES = ["/", "./", "../", "~/"]
SEPARATORS = ["/", "\\"]

def _rand(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]

def _maybe(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _random_ext(r: random.Random) -> str:
    ext = _rand(r, COMMON_EXTS)
    # Occasionally uppercase or mixed case
    style = r.randint(0, 3)
    if style == 1:
        return ext.upper()
    if style == 2:
        return ext.capitalize()
    return ext

def _random_basename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = r.randint(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        return _rand(r, EDGE_BASENAMES)
    if choice == 1:
        return _rand(r, UNICODE_NAMES)
    if choice == 2:
        # dotfile with extension sometimes
        name = "." + _rand(r, ["config", "env", "vimrc", "gitconfig", "hidden"]) \
               + (_maybe(r, 0.5) and ("." + _random_ext(r)) or "")
        return name
    if choice == 3:
        # numeric or UUID-like
        if _maybe(r, 0.5):
            return str(r.randrange(0, 1_000_000))
        # UUID-ish
        parts = [8,4,4,4,12]
        return "-".join(''.join(r.choice(string.hexdigits.lower()) for _ in range(n)) for n in parts)
    if choice == 4:
        # random word
        alph = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
        ln = r.randint(1, 16)
        return ''.join(r.choice(alph) for _ in range(ln))
    if choice == 5:
        # multi-dot names
        words = ["backup", "data", "archive", "report", "summer", "2025", "final", "v1"]
        k = r.randint(2, 4)
        base = '.'.join(_rand(r, words) for _ in range(k))
        return base
    # default: compound archive
    return "archive.tar"  # will likely get another extension appended

def _with_extension(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # Decide whether to attach 0, 1, or compound extensions
    mode = r.randint(0, 4)
    if mode == 0:
        return base  # no extension
    if mode == 1:
        return f"{base}.{_random_ext(r)}"
    if mode == 2:
        # compound compressed archive
        return f"{base}.tar.{_rand(r, ['gz','bz2','xz','zst'])}"
    if mode == 3:
        # double ambiguous
        return f"{base}.{_random_ext(r)}.{_random_ext(r)}"
    # parameter-like suffix or query-like tail that some logic should ignore
    tail = _rand(r, [";charset=utf-8", "?download=1", "#fragment", ";v=1"])
    return f"{base}.{_random_ext(r)}{tail}"

def _random_dir_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = r.randint(0, 5)
    if depth == 0:
        return ""
    # Maybe start with a prefix
    prefix = _rand(r, PREFIXES) if _maybe(r, 0.6) else ""
    sep = _rand(r, SEPARATORS)
    for _ in range(depth):
        comp_choice = r.randint(0, 5)
        if comp_choice == 0:
            parts.append(_rand(r, DIR_COMPONENTS))
        elif comp_choice == 1:
            parts.append(_rand(r, UNICODE_NAMES))
        elif comp_choice == 2:
            parts.append("." + _rand(r, ["cache", "local", "config"]))
        elif comp_choice == 3:
            parts.append(str(r.randrange(1, 100)))
        elif comp_choice == 4:
            parts.append("..")
        else:
            parts.append(''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + "-_ ") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8))))
    path = prefix + sep.join(parts)
    # Ensure trailing separator sometimes
    if _maybe(r, 0.2):
        path += sep
    return path

def _maybe_windows_drive(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if _maybe(r, 0.2):
        drive = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        sep = _rand(r, SEPARATORS)
        return f"{drive}:{sep}"
    return ""

def _maybe_dot_suffix(r: random.Random, name: str) -> str:
    # Add trailing dot(s) or spaces which are corner cases on Windows
    if _maybe(r, 0.1):
        return name + ("." * r.randint(1, 3))
    if _maybe(r, 0.1):
        return name + (" " * r.randint(1, 3))
    return name

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Build filename
    drive = _maybe_windows_drive(r)
    dirpath = _random_dir_path(r)
    sep = _rand(r, SEPARATORS) if (drive or dirpath) else ""

    base = _random_basename(r)
    name = _with_extension(r, base)

    # Occasionally make it a hidden file by prefixing a dot if not already
    if not name.startswith('.') and _maybe(r, 0.15):
        name = "." + name

    # Optional version/locale suffixes
    if _maybe(r, 0.2):
        name += _rand(r, [".en_US", ".KO", ".utf8", ".min", ".backup"])

    # Apply odd casing on the whole name sometimes
    if _maybe(r, 0.1):
        style = r.randint(0, 2)
        if style == 0:
            name = name.upper()
        elif style == 1:
            name = name.capitalize()

    full = f"{drive}{dirpath}{sep}{name}" if (drive or dirpath) else name

    # Maybe add trailing dot/space edge
    full = _maybe_dot_suffix(r, full)

    # Ensure non-empty; fall back
    if not full:
        full = "a"

    # Limit overall size
    if len(full) > 4000:
        full = full[:4000]

    # Return as bytes; C++ stub will convert into std::string and ensure NUL termination
    return full.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for MIME-like strings suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR in xdg-mime fuzzers.
# We focus on producing valid, diverse, and interesting MIME type strings of the
# form type/subtype with optional trees, suffixes, and parameters. We avoid NULs
# inside and keep under 4096 bytes total.

_TOP_LEVEL_TYPES = [
    "application", "audio", "example", "font", "image", "message",
    "model", "multipart", "text", "video"
]

# Common subtypes by top-level; used to produce known-good and edge-case combos
_KNOWN_SUBTYPES = {
    "application": [
        "octet-stream", "json", "xml", "x-www-form-urlencoded", "pdf",
        "zip", "x-sharedlib", "x-executable", "javascript", "x-7z-compressed",
        "x-tar", "x-bzip2", "x-xz", "pgp-encrypted"
    ],
    "audio": ["mpeg", "ogg", "wav", "flac", "webm", "aac"],
    "font": ["woff", "woff2", "otf", "ttf", "collection"],
    "image": ["png", "jpeg", "gif", "bmp", "webp", "tiff", "svg+xml", "heif"],
    "message": ["rfc822", "partial"],
    "model": ["gltf+json", "stl", "obj", "vnd.collada+xml"],
    "multipart": ["mixed", "alternative", "form-data", "byteranges"],
    "text": [
        "plain", "html", "csv", "css", "xml", "x-python", "x-c",
        "markdown", "vcard", "calendar"
    ],
    "video": ["mp4", "webm", "ogg", "x-msvideo", "quicktime"]
}

_VENDOR_PREFIXES = [
    "vnd", "prs", "x"
]

# Parameter names/values for text/* and others to exercise parsers that may accept them
_PARAM_CANDIDATES = [
    ("charset", ["utf-8", "us-ascii", "iso-8859-1"]),
    ("format", ["flowed", "delsp"]),
    ("boundary", ["----boundary", "abc123", "=_mixed"]),
    ("version", ["1", "2.0"]) 
]

# Alias/canonicalization triggers commonly present in shared-mime-info
_ALIASY = [
    "text/x-c", "text/x-python", "application/x-javascript", "image/x-ms-bmp",
    "application/x-zip-compressed", "image/jpg", "text/x-markdown"
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    alpha = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-._"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # ensure doesn't start with '.' to avoid odd paths, but allow hyphen
    first_alpha = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    s = rng.choice(first_alpha)
    s += ''.join(rng.choice(alpha) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s

def _maybe_suffix(rng: random.Random, subtype: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes add +suffix (e.g., application/ld+json, image/svg+xml)
    if rng.random() < 0.35 and "+" not in subtype:
        suffix = _rand_choice(rng, ["xml", "json", "zip", "ber", "cbor", "gzip"]) 
        return f"{subtype}+{suffix}"
    return subtype

def _maybe_vendor_tree(rng: random.Random, subtype: str) -> str:
    # Chance to prepend vnd., prs., or x- style trees
    if rng.random() < 0.40 and not subtype.startswith(tuple(p + "." for p in _VENDOR_PREFIXES)):
        pref = _rand_choice(rng, _VENDOR_PREFIXES)
        # Some trees use hyphen rather than dot; both are seen in practice
        joiner = "." if rng.random() < 0.6 else "-"
        org = _rand_token(rng, 2, 10)
        rest = subtype
        # Occasionally craft subtype purely under tree
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            rest = _rand_token(rng, 2, 10)
        return f"{pref}{joiner}{org}.{rest}" if joiner == "-" else f"{pref}.{org}.{rest}"
    return subtype

def _maybe_params(rng: random.Random, mime: str) -> str:
    # While many lib APIs ignore parameters, some accept them; include occasionally
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        count = rng.randint(1, 2)
        parts = []
        for _ in range(count):
            name, vals = _rand_choice(rng, _PARAM_CANDIDATES)
            val = _rand_choice(rng, vals)
            # quote sometimes
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                val = f'"{val}"'
            parts.append(f"{name}={val}")
        return mime + "; " + "; ".join(parts)
    return mime

def _build_mime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose between known aliases, known good combinations, and random novel ones
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.20:
        # Use alias-like strings to tickle unalias and equality
        return _rand_choice(rng, _ALIASY)
    elif mode < 0.70:
        t = _rand_choice(rng, _TOP_LEVEL_TYPES)
        sub = _rand_choice(rng, _KNOWN_SUBTYPES.get(t, ["plain"]))
        sub = _maybe_suffix(rng, sub)
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            sub = _maybe_vendor_tree(rng, sub)
        mime = f"{t}/{sub}"
        return _maybe_params(rng, mime)
    else:
        # Construct random but valid-looking type/subtype
        t = _rand_choice(rng, _TOP_LEVEL_TYPES + ["x-" + _rand_token(rng, 3, 8)])
        sub = _rand_token(rng, 3, 14)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            sub = _maybe_suffix(rng, sub)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            sub = _maybe_vendor_tree(rng, sub)
        mime = f"{t}/{sub}"
        return _maybe_params(rng, mime)

def _mix_pair(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # Return a pair potentially sharing media type to exercise media_type_equal
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        t = _rand_choice(rng, _TOP_LEVEL_TYPES)
        a = f"{t}/{_rand_choice(rng, _KNOWN_SUBTYPES.get(t, ['plain']))}"
        b = f"{t}/{_rand_choice(rng, _KNOWN_SUBTYPES.get(t, ['plain']))}"
        return a, b
    else:
        return _build_mime(rng), _build_mime(rng)

def _compose_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    items: List[str] = []
    # Seed with canonical types
    canon = [
        "text/plain", "image/png", "application/octet-stream", "application/json",
        "text/html", "image/jpeg", "application/xml", "application/zip"
    ]
    items.extend(canon)

    # Include aliasy forms
    items.extend(_ALIASY)

    # A couple with parameters
    items.append("text/plain; charset=utf-8")
    items.append("multipart/form-data; boundary=----boundary")

    # Pairs for equality/media-type checks
    for _ in range(4):
        a, b = _mix_pair(rng)
        items.append(a)
        items.append(b)

    # More random variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(6, 12)):
        items.append(_build_mime(rng))

    # Ensure reasonable uniqueness while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[str] = []
    for s in items:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq

def _encode_concatenated(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join MIME strings with newlines; FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically consumes arbitrary
    # strings, and the harness picks slices. Providing a corpus separated by newlines
    # gives the fuzzer multiple candidates in one buffer.
    blob = ("\n".join(strings)).encode("utf-8")
    # Bound size to <= 4096 bytes by truncating at a newline boundary if needed
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        cut = blob[:4096].rfind(b"\n")
        if cut == -1:
            return blob[:4096]
        return blob[:cut]
    return blob

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = _compose_corpus(rng)
    return _encode_concatenated(strings)
